ledger.x: 1600: Elizabeth I's charter founds the East India Company.
1639: the Company buys Madras.
1668: the Crown passes Bombay to the Company.
1690: Fort St David.
1696: Fort William at Calcutta.
23 June 1757: Plassey.
June 1757: Bengal and Bihar under a Company puppet.
1759: Masulipatnam.
1760: Mir Qasim, installed 'with the support of the British East India Company', 'granted it the right to collect revenue of the districts of Burdwan, Midnapore and Chittagong'.
1763: the Chingleput jaghire, 'obtained in 1763, was the first district in the Madras Presidency'.
16 August 1765: the Nawab's Bengal ceases to be a plain client.
16 August 1765: the diwani of Bengal and Bihar.
1768: the Nizam gives up the Northern Circars.
1773: Calcutta becomes the Company's capital.
1773: Cooch Behar a protectorate of the East India Company.
1782: Salsette.
1788: Guntur.
1789: the Andaman settlement.
26 October 1790: Coorg becomes a British protectorate, after Mysore's occupation of 1780-1788.
1791: Cochin becomes a protected state.
1791: the colony leaves Chatham Island.
1791: the colony at Port Cornwallis.
1792: Dindigul.
March 1792: Tipu loses half his kingdom.
1794: Jaipur under British protection ('Jaipur (1794) & Travancore (1795) come under British protection').
1795: Travancore under British protection.
May 1796: the Andaman station is abandoned.
1798: Hyderabad signs the first subsidiary alliance.
4 May 1799: Seringapatam falls.
1799: the Wadiyars restored under a subsidiary alliance.
1799: Thanjavur passes to the Company.
1799: the titular rajah keeps a remnant.
1800: the Ceded Districts.
1800: 'The British annexed Surat in 1800.'
1801: the Carnatic.
1801: the Ceded Provinces.
1801: Awadh enters a subsidiary alliance ('Tanjore (1799), Awadh (1801), the Peshwa (1802)').
1802: the Peshwa signs at Bassein ('the Peshwa (1802)'; the Second Anglo-Maratha War page: Baji Rao II signed the Treaty of Bassein in December 1802, 'the death knell of the Maratha Empire').
1803: the Bhonsle of Nagpur ('the Bhonsle kingdom (1803), Scindia (1804), Singrauli (1814)').
September 1803: Lake takes Delhi and Wellesley wins at Assaye.
17 December 1803: Deogaon.
30 December 1803: Surji-Anjangaon.
30 December 1803: the Delhi-Doab campaign ends with Surji-Anjangaon.
1804: Scindia enters a subsidiary alliance.
1809: 'Tripura became a British protectorate' (Hill Tippera, a subsidiary alliance until the Indian Independence Act 1947).
1 November 1814: the Anglo-Nepalese War begins ('1 November 1814 to 4 March 1816').
1815: the Cis-Sutlej Hill States ('Cis-Sutlej Hill States (1815)' among the states under British protection); the lands are the researcher's reading (the Simla hills).
4 March 1816: the Treaty of Sugauli is 'formally ratified on 4 March 1816'.
4 March 1816: Sugauli.
1816: Tehri Garhwal becomes a princely state under the Company.
1817: the Rajputana states ('States of Rajputana accept British suzerainty (1817)'; Jaipur and Jodhpur sign subsidiary alliances in 1818).
ledger.cp: Rajputana states (Jodhpur, Udaipur, Bikaner, Kota, Bundi and the rest)

ledger.x: 10 February 1817: the Treaty of Titalia.
5 November 1817: the Third Anglo-Maratha War begins; 'Treaty of Gwalior (5 November 1817): Shinde surrendered Rajasthan to the British'.
1818: the Saugor and Nerbudda Territories.
1818: Cutch accepts British suzerainty ('Cutch accepts British suzerainty (1818)').
6 January 1818: Treaty of Mandeswar.
3 June 1818: the Peshwa's subsidiary state ends.
3 June 1818: the Peshwa's dominions annexed.
3 June 1818: the Peshwa's war ends with his surrender (the war formally to 9 April 1819).
25 June 1818: Ajmer.
1819: the Gaikwads of Baroda accept British suzerainty ('Gaikwads of Baroda accept British suzerainty (1819)').
May 1823: Merwara.
1824: 'From 1824, Manipur became a British protectorate.'
5 March 1824: the First Anglo-Burmese War begins; Rangoon is entered on 11 May 1824.
24 February 1826: Yandabo.
24 February 1826: the Treaty of Yandabo ends the war.
1831: Mysore annexed.
1831-1881: the Company, and after 1858 the Crown, administers Mysore for the Wadiyars.
1832: the Cachar plains.
ledger.cp: Dimasa Kachari kingdom of Cachar (no dossier)

ledger.x: 1833: Bahawalpur accepts British suzerainty ('Bahawalpur accepts British Suzerainty (1833)').
April 1833: Upper Assam is handed to a protected prince.
April 1833: Purandar Singha rules Upper Assam as a protected prince 'on a stipulated tribute of 50,000 rupees'.
1834: the North Cachar hills.
ledger.cp: Dimasa Kachari kingdom of Cachar (no dossier)

ledger.x: 1834: 'Coorg annexed (1834).'
10 April 1834: the Raja of Coorg surrenders at Madikeri; Coorg is annexed (see the gain of 1834).
1835: Darjeeling.
15 March 1835: Jaintia.
September 1838: the protected principality ends.
September 1838: Upper Assam annexed again ('the annexation of Upper Assam to the territories of the British East India Company').
1839: 'The Kurnool kingdom was annexed in 1839 and was constituted as a separate district.'
1839: Aden. 'Aden is captured by Company (1839)'; 'Aden including Socotra were placed under Bombay in 1839'. Outside South Asia; kept because the pages give the year and the place.
13 November 1839: the British storm Kalat ('Siege of Kalat (13 November 1839)'); the occupation is recorded in khanate-of-kalat.
1841: the occupation ends.
17 February 1843: Miani.
24 March 1843 and after: Sindh.
24 March 1843: the Battle of Hyderabad closes the Sindh campaign.
1846: the First Anglo-Sikh War settlement.
1846: Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh.
1848: 'the Company took over the princely states of Satara (1848)' under the doctrine of lapse.
18 April 1848: the Second Anglo-Sikh War begins at Multan ('18 April 1848 - 29 March 1849').
1849: 'Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849)' annexed under the doctrine of lapse.
1849: Jaitpur annexed under the doctrine of lapse.
29 March 1849: the war ends; annexation proclaimed 2 April.
2 April 1849: the Punjab.
5 April 1852: the Second Anglo-Burmese War begins; Martaban is taken on 5 April, Rangoon on 12 April.
1853: Nagpur lapses.
1853: Nagpur annexed under the doctrine of lapse.
20 January 1853: Pegu.
20 January 1853: the war ends with the proclamation of annexation.
1854: Jhansi annexed under the doctrine of lapse (table 1853).
1855: the titular principality lapses.
1855: the fort and its surroundings, the last of the titular principality, are annexed ('Thanjavur was annexed in 1855'); the land round it had been the Company's since 1799.
1856: Oudh annexed ('In 1854 Berar was annexed, and the state of Oudh two years later'; 'annexed by Dalhousie under the pretext of mis-governance').
1856: Oudh annexed by Dalhousie ('Annexation of Berar (1853) and Awadh (1856)').
10 May 1857: the Meerut mutiny.
November 1857: Port Blair is settled again.
20 June 1858: 'contained only with the rebels' defeat in Gwalior on 20 June 1858'; hostilities were not formally declared over until 8 July 1859.

wars.name: Battle of Plassey
wars.outcome: Company victory on 23 June 1757; Mir Jafar installed as Nawab; the land around Calcutta ceded.

wars.name: Battle of Buxar
wars.outcome: Company victory in 1764 over Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II; the Treaty of Allahabad of 16 August 1765 gave the diwani and left Awadh with Shuja-ud-Daula but without Allahabad and Kora.

wars.name: First Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Madras; the page names no cession.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Mangalore, 11 March 1784, 'restored the status quo ante bellum'.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Seringapatam, 18 March 1792: Mysore lost about one half of its territory to the allies, including Malabar and Salem to the Company.

wars.name: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: Seringapatam stormed on 4 May 1799; Tipu killed; Coimbatore and Dakshina Kannada to the Company; the Wadiyars restored under a subsidiary alliance.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War
wars.outcome: Company victory (8 August 1803 - 24 December 1805): Cuttack from the Bhonsle (Deogaon), the Doab, Delhi and Agra from Scindia (Surji-Anjangaon, 30 December 1803); Rajghat (24 December 1805) made Holkar give up Tonk, Rampura and Bundi.

wars.name: Anglo-Nepalese War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Sugauli, ratified 4 March 1816: Kumaon, Garhwal and the western Terai and the strip to the Teesta to the Company; some Terai lands returned later in 1816.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Maratha War
wars.outcome: 5 November 1817 - 9 April 1819: Peshwa surrendered 3 June 1818 and his dominions were annexed to Bombay; Holkar subsidiary at Mandeswar (6 January 1818); the Company controlled 'virtually all of present-day India south of the Sutlej'.

wars.name: First Anglo-Burmese War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Yandabo, 24 February 1826: Assam, Manipur, Arakan and Tenasserim ceded.

wars.name: Conquest of Sindh
wars.outcome: Miani (17 February 1843) and Hyderabad (24 March 1843); Sindh annexed; the Amirs of Hyderabad exiled.

wars.name: First Anglo-Sikh War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Bhairowal / Lahore (1846): the Jullundur Doab ceded; Kashmir and Jammu to Gulab Singh by sale.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Sikh War
wars.outcome: 18 April 1848 - 29 March 1849; Multan stormed 2 January 1849, Gujrat won 21 February 1849; Punjab annexed 2 April 1849.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Burmese War
wars.outcome: 5 April 1852 - 20 January 1853: Pegu province annexed by proclamation of 20 January 1853.

wars.name: Indian Rebellion of 1857
wars.outcome: 10 May 1857 - 20 June 1858 (formally 8 July 1859): the Company wins; the Government of India Act 1858 ends the Company's rule on 1 November 1858.

wars.name: British-Koch war against Bhutan
wars.outcome: A British-Koch coalition captured the capital in 1772; the British negotiated a peace with Bhutan on 25 April 1774, and Cooch Behar became a Company protectorate (infobox 1773-1858).

certainty.note: Factories and small enclaves with no surveyed boundary; the Maratha Ditch line at Calcutta is the only defined edge.
The Company's land follows districts and revenue grants; no page opened draws a boundary, and the ring of subsidiary states is not delimited.
Treaty and annexation lines: Sugauli (4 March 1816) in the north, Yandabo (24 February 1826), the Sutlej frontier and the 1849 Punjab districts; the Sindh and Punjab-NWFP frontier tracts stay soft.
